sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 1384 ± 233.9 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: ELISA for surface expression: surface display confirmed (L6). Confocal microscopy showing predominant plasma membrane distribution in hippocampal neurons confirmed (L3/L4). FLAG affinity purification confirmed expression (L2). No ligand-binding or signaling functional assay reported in any supporting clip.
sites.rationale: CHRM2 has no annotated signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–22 as extracellular and TM1 begins at residue 23, leaving exactly one extracellular terminus (the N-terminus). The tag therefore prepends before Met1 (insert_after_residue=0), 22 residues from the TM1 boundary, well within the ≥3-residue requirement. Three independent papers (L6 HA/ELISA, L2 FLAG/purification, L3–L5 GFP-SEP/confocal) all report N-terminal tags on the full-length membrane-anchored receptor with confirmed surface display, converging on this single junction. Position is topology-derived because no clip names a specific residue number. SP-HA-M2R-WT construct: an exogenous signal peptide followed by an HA tag was cloned N-terminally to the full-length wild-type human M2 receptor; after SP cleavage the HA tag is displayed at the extracellular N-terminus. Construct used in ELISA assays for surface expression in transfected cells (PMC12935549). Corroborated by L2 (FLAG at N-terminus, FLAG-affinity purification, PMC4020789) and L3/L4/L5 (GFP/SEP at N-terminus, confocal PM distribution in hippocampal neurons, PMC6283979).

sources.claim: For the ELISA assay, an HA-tag was cloned N-terminally to the WT receptor, resulting in SP-HA-M 2 R-WT, using primers 3 and 11, and 1 and 12.

literature_notes: All ledger lines supporting a surface tag (L2, L3, L4, L5, L6) converge on the same N-terminal extracellular junction (prepend before Met1); they are not separate junctions and are therefore reported as one site. L6 is chosen as the primary supporting clip because it uses a short epitope tag (HA) and a direct surface-expression assay (ELISA), most analogous to the intended ALFA-tag application. L2 (FLAG) and L3/L4/L5 (GFP/SEP, PM confocal) are noted as corroborating evidence from independent publications. No ledger line reports a tag in any of the three short extracellular loops (ECL1 81–97, ECL2 163–184, ECL3 410–422), so no internal sites are proposed. The C-terminal intracellular tail (444–466) and the large ICL3 (208–388) are covered in other_positions.

literature_other_positions.note: T4 lysozyme (residues 2–161) was inserted into ICL3 replacing M2 residues 218–376 for structural studies; ICL3 (208–388) is intracellular and this is not a surface tag site.
eGFP fused to the C-terminus of full-length M2R (SP-M2R-WT-eGFP); the C-terminus (residues 444–466) is intracellular, so this is not a surface tag site.
